geometries.note: the arm `robot_parameters.json` ships, whose equal links make the fold-back clause reachable and whose `(L1 - L2) ^ 2` is zero make the inner band edge attainable only by folding the second link back onto the first
geometries.name: shipped

geometries.note: the forward-chain corpus's second arm; `a1 = 0` puts the frame-1 origin on the base rotation axis, which is what exercises `leOfRadical`'s `k = 0` arm, and `linkOne ≠ linkTwo` makes the fold-back clause unreachable on it
geometries.name: short_arm

entries.note: rho = 0: the wrist centre on the base rotation axis, `NonDegenerate`'s first clause negated. Three of the four comparisons are decided by a sign alone - two of them by `m ≤ 0` on the `k > 0` side - and the two that do square find `k * k * rho = 0`, which they can only get right because they compare `m * m ≥ 0 ∈ ...` the right way round.
entries.name: shipped/wrist_center_on_base_axis

entries.note: rho = 0 again, at a height: `q σ = -a1` on both branches, and `q ^ 2 + h ^ 2` is `500` - well inside the band - where the case below has it exactly at the inner edge. An off-singularity rotation, so the two halves of the plan are seen to be independent.
entries.name: shipped/wrist_center_on_base_axis_above_the_frame_one_origin

entries.note: The fold-back: with `r = 10` the centre `(10, 0, 40)` is the frame-1 origin itself, `q +1 = r - a1 = 0`, `h = 0`, and `linkOne = linkTwo`. Only `σ = +1` satisfies `radicalEqZero`'s sign half `alpha * beta ≤ 0`: `beta = -2 * σ * a1` is `-20` there and `+20` on `σ = -1`, against `alpha = 200 > 0`, so `fold_back` is `[true, false]` and the case pins which shoulder owns the fold. The same comparison is the lower band edge hit exactly - `q +1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 0 = (L1 - L2) ^ 2` - and it reaches it through the sign-care arm at that arm's own boundary, `k * k * rho = m * m = 40000`.
entries.name: shipped/the_fold_back

entries.note: The fold-back's neighbour, a millionth of a unit higher: `q +1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2` is `10 ^ -12` instead of `0`, so every elbow decision is the fold-back's - the pose is still reachable on both branches - and the plan differs from it in one field only, `fold_back`, which is now `[false, false]`. This is the case that pins the clause as `h = 0` exactly rather than as a small height, and it is also an instance of the sign-care arm's strict inequality: `m * m = 40000 + ... > k * k * rho = 40000`.
entries.name: shipped/the_fold_back_neighbour_above

entries.note: The fold-back's height with `rho = 50`, which is not a rational square, so the decision is made in `Q(sqrt 50)` and `√50` is never needed: the lower-edge comparison of the `+1` branch is `m = -150 ≤ -20 * sqrt 50` decided as `k * k * rho = 20000 ≤ m * m = 22500`, strictly - a `≤` in place of the `≥` there would drop a reachable pose, which is the sign care this case exists to catch.
entries.name: shipped/a_non_square_radius

entries.note: Well inside on both branches: `rho = 3600 = 60 ^ 2` off the x axis, `q +1 = 50` and `q -1 = -70`, so `q +1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 2500` and `q -1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 4900` are both inside `[0, 6400]` with room to spare. The `k = 0` arm is the one this arm never takes: both lower-edge comparisons reach `m ≤ 0` with `k ≠ 0` and decide on the sign.
entries.name: shipped/well_inside_the_band_off_axis

entries.note: The outer band edge approached from inside by a millionth of a unit: `alpha - 6400 = 200 - 160 / 10 ^ 6 + 10 ^ -12 > 0`, so the `+1` branch's upper comparison takes the arm that decides by squaring - `m * m ≤ k * k * rho`, strictly here - and says reachable, while `σ = -1`, twenty units further out, is dropped.
entries.name: shipped/inside_the_upper_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: The upper band edge hit exactly: `q +1 = 0` with `h = 80 = L1 + L2`, so `q +1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 6400` and the arm is stretched straight out. `Set.Icc (-1) 1` includes its ends, so the `+1` branch is reachable, and the squaring arm meets it at `m * m = k * k * rho = 40000` exactly. `σ = -1` at `q -1 = -20` has `6800 > 6400` and is dropped, so one pose carries both answers. With `a1 ≠ 0` an exact edge forces `rho` to be a rational square - the edge equation is linear in `r = sqrt rho`, so `r` must be rational to hold at a rational centre - and here it is `10`.
entries.name: shipped/the_upper_edge_exactly

entries.note: The same edge from outside, by the same millionth: the `+1` branch's squaring arm now has `m * m > k * k * rho` and the branch is dropped, and `σ = -1` is dropped with it, so `candidate_count` is 0. With the two cases above it fixes the band as the closed interval `[0, 6400]` at three heights one millionth apart: a strict inequality at either end of the test gets one of the three wrong.
entries.name: shipped/outside_the_upper_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: The same edge from the other shoulder branch: `(70, 0, 40)` puts `q -1 = -80` on the edge and leaves `σ = +1`, at `q +1 = 60`, strictly inside. The edge comparison is then `m = alpha - 6400 = -1400 ≤ 0` with `k = -20 < 0` - the sign-care arm - and it meets that arm's boundary `k * k * rho = m * m = 1960000` exactly, where the `+1` edge case meets the squaring arm's. The two `m * m` comparisons of the band are therefore pinned at equality, one by each shoulder branch.
entries.name: shipped/the_upper_edge_exactly_mirrored

entries.note: rho = 0 with `h = 100`: the wrist centre is on the base axis, so `radius_is_zero` and `wrist_center_on_base_axis` are true, and `q σ ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 10100` is past `(L1 + L2) ^ 2 = 6400`, so both branches are dropped and the count is 0. The anchor is a decision about `rho` alone and says nothing about reachability.
entries.name: shipped/on_the_base_axis_out_of_reach

entries.note: The `+1` upper edge again, with `y ≠ 0` and both halves of the centre rational rather than integral: `rho = 3364 = 58 ^ 2`, `q +1 = 48`, `h = 64`. `(48, 64)` is a Pythagorean point, so `q +1 ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 6400` exactly and `m * m = k * k * rho` again holds with equality; `σ = -1`, at `q -1 = -68`, has `8720 > 6400` and is dropped.
entries.name: shipped/upper_edge_with_an_off_axis_center

entries.note: rho = 0 on the arm with `a1 = 0`: `beta σ = -2 * σ * a1` vanishes on both branches, so all four comparisons take the `k = 0` arm and both shoulder branches read the same band. The centre is the frame-1 origin itself, and with links 30 and 12 it lies inside the inner dead zone: `alpha = 0 < (L1 - L2) ^ 2 = 324`, so `m ≤ 0` is false and the plan is empty. A dead zone is where the inner edge is violated on the small side.
entries.name: short_arm/wrist_center_on_base_axis

entries.note: A rational-square radius: `rho = 324 = 18 ^ 2` with `alpha = 324 + 400 = 724`, strictly inside `[324, 1764]`. Both routes to the band are available here - the radical route and `elbowCosine` with `r = 18` substituted - and the generator requires them to agree before writing.
entries.name: short_arm/a_square_radius

entries.note: The same geometry and the same height as the case above, with `rho = 2` where that one has `rho = 324`: the decision is unchanged, because with `a1 = 0` the band is `alpha ∈ [324, 1764]` and `alpha` is `402` here against `724` there. `sqrt 2` is irrational, so this decision is made in `Q(sqrt 2)`; the extension is entered and the root is never taken. The radius route is unavailable here, which is the point of the radical route existing at all.
entries.name: short_arm/a_non_square_radius_at_the_same_height

entries.note: The inner band edge from inside, by a millionth of a unit: `alpha = rho + h ^ 2 = 180 + (12 + 10 ^ -6) ^ 2 = 324 + 24 / 10 ^ 6 + 10 ^ -12 > (L1 - L2) ^ 2`, so the lower comparison's `m = 324 - alpha` is negative and the `k = 0` arm's `m ≤ 0` holds. Reachable on both branches, since with `a1 = 0` there is no second answer to compute.
entries.name: short_arm/inside_the_inner_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: The inner band edge hit exactly, with `rho` still not a rational square: `(x, y, h) = (12, 6, 12)` is the rational sphere point `18 * (2/3, 1/3, 2/3)`, so `rho + h ^ 2 = 180 + 144 = 324 = (L1 - L2) ^ 2` and the comparison's `m` is exactly `0`. `m ≤ 0` includes its end, so the pose is reachable - a strict `<` there would report an arm that folds the second link back exactly onto the first as out of reach. With `a1 = 0` the edge equation has no `r` in it, so nothing forces `rho` to be a square here as it does on the `shipped` edges.
entries.name: short_arm/the_inner_edge_exactly

entries.note: The inner dead zone, a millionth inside it: `alpha = 324 - 24 / 10 ^ 6 + 10 ^ -12 < (L1 - L2) ^ 2`, so `m = 324 - alpha > 0` and the `k = 0` arm's `m ≤ 0` returns false. Both branches are dropped and the count is 0. With the two cases above it pins the inner edge as a boundary of the band rather than as an artefact of where the link lengths happen to fall.
entries.name: short_arm/outside_the_inner_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: The outer band edge from inside, by a millionth: `rho = 980` and `q ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 980 + (28 - 10 ^ -6) ^ 2 = 1764 - 56 / 10 ^ 6 + 10 ^ -12 < (L1 + L2) ^ 2`, so the upper comparison's `m = alpha - 1764` is negative and the `k = 0` arm's `m ≤ 0` holds.
entries.name: short_arm/inside_the_outer_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: The outer band edge hit exactly: `(x, y, h) = (28, 14, 28)` is `42 * (2/3, 1/3, 2/3)`, so `rho = 980` and `q ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 980 + 784 = 1764 = (L1 + L2) ^ 2` with the upper comparison's `m` exactly `0`. Reachable - the same fact as the `shipped` upper edge with `a1 = 0`, so no rational radius is needed for the edge to be hit.
entries.name: short_arm/the_outer_edge_exactly

entries.note: Past the outer edge by a millionth: `q ^ 2 + h ^ 2 = 1764 + 56 / 10 ^ 6 + 10 ^ -12`, the upper comparison's `m > 0` fails `m ≤ 0`, and both branches are dropped. The three `short_arm` edge cases at heights one millionth apart pin the outer edge of this arm the way the three `shipped` ones pin its own.
entries.name: short_arm/outside_the_outer_edge_by_a_hair

entries.note: Well inside, with a square radius and neither link at an extreme: `rho = 900 = 30 ^ 2`, `h = 15` and `alpha = 1125`, between `324` and `1764` with room to spare. The arm reaches the same band from both shoulder branches, which is what `a1 = 0` means.
entries.name: short_arm/well_inside_the_band

conventions: Each entry is a wrist centre `(x4, y4, z4)` and the relative rotation `R_3^6` of a target pose, both exact rationals, and the branch plan `InverseKinematics`'s predicates decide for them. `radius_is_zero` is `shoulderRadius g T = 0`, the wrist centre on the base rotation axis, which is `NonDegenerate`'s first clause negated; `wrist_center_on_base_axis` is the same predicate as `Degeneracy` carries it, and a consumer should find the two equal. `elbow_branches` is `elbowBranches g T σ` per shoulder branch, in generation order σ = +1 then -1, each the pair of elbow labels [1, -1] with kept or not: the Lean test is one band membership, so the pair is kept together or not at all. `fold_back` is `Degeneracy.fold_back` per shoulder branch, `NonDegenerate`'s second clause negated. `wrist_singular` is `wristIsSingular` for the entry's rotation, exact because `hypot (Q 0 2) (Q 1 2) = 0` holds exactly when both entries vanish. `candidate_count` is two wrist labels for every kept elbow branch, which is `length_solutions_le_eight`'s bound computed. The band test behind `elbow_branches` is a comparison in the quadratic extension Q(sqrt rho), with `rho = x4^2 + y4^2`: the generator isolates the radical and squares with sign care, so no square root is ever evaluated and every value here is exact. `branch` names which of the five arms a case is written for (`k_zero`; `m_nonpos_k_pos`; `m_nonpos_k_neg`, the one that squares only after negating; `m_pos_k_pos`; `m_pos_k_neg`) and a case whose declared arm none of its four comparisons enters is not written at all. `radius` is the non-negative rational square root of `rho` when there is one and null otherwise: it is what lets the generator re-derive the band the long way round, through `elbowCosine`, and no consumer needs it. Geometry is named by the kinematic dimensions: `a1` is `Geometry.a1`, `d1` is `Geometry.d1`, `link_one` is `linkOne` (the DH table's `a2`) and `link_two` is `linkTwo` (`d4`); no case reads the tool offset, so these geometries do not carry one. Two cases carry a matrix that is not a rotation - one entry of the third column zero and the other not - because that is the only witness that `wrist_plan_exact` is a conjunction, and `wristRotation`'s third column vanishes in both entries at once; the rest are ZYZ products with rational cosine/sine pairs, which the generator re-derives before writing. Every numeral is an exact integer or "num/den" string, never a JSON number.
